correctness.rationale: Probability normalization follows from Cauchy's projection formula and the exact beta integral in dimension d−1. The Euclidean inradius is an exact concave-simplex minimum at coordinate vertices. Strict-concavity KKT conditions completely resolve the circumradius and all maximizing normals with a unique multiplier; no numerical optimizer is used in proof. Diagonal support evaluation plus max-weight averaging yields the all-dimensional sharp ratio and rigid cube equality. Two phase formulas and their second-derivative jump are elementary substitutions. Diagnostic code was executed from the actual accompanying file and passed 500 independent numerical constrained optimizations and 1,500 quadrature comparisons; finite checks are not universal proof.

value.rationale: Euclidean radius extrema are natural roundness invariants for Radon mean-section images. Every positive weight tuple corresponds to a genuine orthotope, making the KKT phase classification a complete natural family, including an exact nondifferentiability transition in dimension 3. The cube-only sharp global roundness bound supplies rigorous anisotropy rigidity and a practical dimension-dependent benchmark for geometric tomography, beyond mere computation or repetition of known dice geometry.
